payload.name: pressed-voice
payload.scope: People made pressed voice as a classification category to name the phonation mode of excessive glottal contact - hyperfunctional phonation - so that laryngology can tell it apart from modal and breathy phonation in voice-disorder assessment and voice therapy.

definition.body: Pressed voice (pressed phonation, hyperfunctional phonation) is a classification category for a mode of voiced phonation defined by a specific glottal configuration: the vocal folds are pressed together with excessive medial compression, so that each cycle carries a prolonged closed phase and an abrupt, steep opening. Its parameters are: (1) the glottal configuration - excessive medial compression of the folds with prolonged complete closure during each vibration cycle, (2) the cycle signature - a shortened open phase and a lengthened closed phase relative to the fundamental period (a high contact quotient, a low open quotient), a short rise time, and a steep flow declination, (3) the acoustic signature - a harsh, strained, or pressed timbre with reduced harmonic-to-noise contrast and reduced glottal airflow. It persists as a named mode of the phonation-mode taxonomy: documented in laryngology (spastic and hyperfunctional dysphonia, muscle-tension dysphonia), used in voice-disorder assessment and voice therapy, and maintained alongside modal, breathy, falsetto, creaky, and whisper phonation. e.g.: the pressed (hyperfunctional) category in a voice-disorder assessment of muscle-tension dysphonia; the pressed-voice label in a laryngoscopy report of spastic dysphonia; the pressed category in Sundberg's five-mode phonation inventory | not: creaky voice (low-frequency implosive vibration, a different mode); breathy voice (incomplete closure with noise leak, a different mode); modal phonation (complete closure at modal timing, a different mode) [formal: vox compressa | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes]
